text: Continuous integration is a software development practice where team members frequently merge their code changes into a shared main branch. Each time new code is added, a CI pipeline automatically builds the software and runs a series of tests. This automated process helps catch issues early, before they become bigger problems. For example, if a developer's change accidentally breaks a feature, the tests will fail immediately, and the team can fix it quickly. By running automated builds and tests regularly, teams can maintain a stable codebase and collaborate more effectively. This saves time and reduces the risk of major bugs reaching production.
